# Exit codes of a nanodregg unit

A unit runs `nd-supervise … -- host …`. nd-supervise passes the child's code through, so one
code space holds both tables: `host` (Host.Status, below 64) and nd-supervise's own
(Protocol.SupervisorExit, 64 and up). `host` prints `refused NAME` or `exit NAME` on stderr.

## host

| code | name | class | systemd | operator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | eof | done | stays stopped (success) | nothing: the supervisor closed the stream |
| 3 | uncertain | restart | restarted after 2 s; failed past 5 starts in 120 s | automatic; replies were `uncertain`, clients look their calls up |
| 4 | fuel | restart | restarted after 2 s; failed past 5 starts in 120 s | never an exit: a fuel round reopens in process (D4); seen from outside, a defect: report to HOST |
| 5 | sealIo | restart | restarted after 2 s; failed past 5 starts in 120 s | automatic; check the disk's space and errors |
| 6 | ioServing | restart | restarted after 2 s; failed past 5 starts in 120 s | automatic; an IO error after the open: check the disk |
| 8 | usage | fatal | stopped (RestartPreventExitStatus) | fix the unit's argv |
| 9 | entropy | fatal | stopped (RestartPreventExitStatus) | the OS random source failed: do not genesis on this box |
| 10 | recordTooLarge | fatal | stopped (RestartPreventExitStatus) | a defect or the HOST-14 design limit: report to HOST |
| 11 | worldTooLarge | fatal | stopped (RestartPreventExitStatus) | a defect or the HOST-14 design limit: report to HOST |

## nd-supervise

| code | name | class | systemd | operator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | refusedAtLaunch | fatal | stopped (RestartPreventExitStatus) | refused before the child ran (nothing hidden, an unreadable argument, a socket it cannot bind, the sandbox's policy or mechanism): fix the unit or the box; the reason is on stderr |
| 65 | childUnroutable | fatal | stopped (RestartPreventExitStatus) | the child wrote a frame the mux cannot route: a defect in the child, report to HOST and CLIENT |
| 66 | childSignaled | restart | restarted after 2 s; failed past 5 starts in 120 s | automatic; the child was killed by a signal (the OOM killer, an operator; on Linux any mechanism exit of 128 or more, bwrap's 128+N); a crash on every start stops at the start limit |
